summary.title: 我正在为多光谱成像相机设计一片可见-近红外双波段分光膜。要求可见光波段 45
summary.question: 我正在为多光谱成像相机设计一片可见-近红外双波段分光膜。要求可见光波段 450-650 nm 尽可能高的反射率（用于 RGB 通道成像），同时近红外波段 700-1000 nm 尽可能高的透过率（用于 NIR 通道），降低通道间串扰。请在 45 度入射、熔融石英基底条件下，仅使用 TiO2 和 SiO2 设计一个平面多层介质膜，膜系总层数不超过 24 层。

problem.compatibility_reason: Request specifies planar isotropic layered media solvable by transfer matrix method.

metrics.rationale: User requires '可见光波段 450-650 nm 尽可能高的反射率（用于 RGB 通道成像）' - high reflectance in visible band for RGB imaging.
User requires '近红外波段 700-1000 nm 尽可能高的透过率（用于 NIR 通道）' - high transmittance in NIR band for NIR imaging.

scoring.metric_rationale: These two metrics directly capture the dual-band dichroic requirement: maximize reflectance in 450-650 nm (visible/RGB) and maximize transmittance in 700-1000 nm (NIR). Together they inherently minimize crosstalk - high reflectance in visible means low transmittance there, and high transmittance in NIR means low reflectance there. I deliberately omit worst_case variants because the user said '尽可能高' (as high as possible) without specifying uniformity across the band, and mean values better reflect overall imaging performance. I omit absorption metrics because dielectric TiO2/SiO2 stacks have negligible absorption, and the user did not mention thermal or loss requirements. The 45° angle is included because the user explicitly stated '45 度入射'. Polarization is omitted because the user did not specify it, and multispectral cameras typically use unpolarized light.
scoring.formula_rationale: The user requires high performance in both the visible and NIR bands equally, with no stated priority for one over the other. Adding the two metrics ensures that the score rewards improvements in either band, encouraging designs that achieve high reflectance for RGB imaging and high transmittance for NIR imaging simultaneously. This sum directly addresses the crosstalk reduction goal because maximizing visible reflectance keeps visible light out of the NIR path, while maximizing NIR transmittance keeps NIR light out of the visible path.

routes.design_principle: Distributed Bragg reflector physics: alternating high/low index layers at quarter-wave optical thickness create constructive interference for reflection in the stopband. routes.title: Quarter-wave TiO2/SiO2 dichroic stack with thickness tuning
routes.termination_reason: LLM explicitly assessed no further benefit after 8 executed rounds (stop_basis=marginal_gains_too_low)
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 24-layer periodic TiO2/SiO2 stack with quarter-wave optical thickness centered at approximately 550 nm will achieve high reflectance in 450-650 nm and high transmittance in 700-1000 nm at 45 degrees incidence, with the band-edge transition sharpness improving as layer thicknesses are optimized away from nominal quarter-wave values.
routes.design_principle: Bragg reflection from a periodic high-low index stack creates a photonic stopband centered at the quarter-wave condition. The stopband width scales with the index contrast (TiO2 ~2.4, SiO2 ~1.46). At oblique incidence, the effective optical thickness decreases by cos(theta_internal), shifting the stopband to shorter wavelengths. Unpolarized performance requires balancing s and p polarization responses.
routes.topology: Air | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica Substrate (24 layers total, 12 HL pairs)
known_risks: Uncertain whether 12 pairs is optimal vs fewer pairs with matching layers - did not check literature for pair-count optimization
Exact TiO2 refractive index dispersion in 450-1000 nm range is recalled approximately, actual dataset may differ
Polarization splitting at 45 degrees may cause visible-band reflectance to differ between s and p - user did not specify polarization state, assumed unpolarized average
Band-edge position may not align perfectly with 650/700 nm boundary without thickness tuning - this is what optimization addresses
Fused silica substrate refractive index (~1.46) is close to SiO2 coating index, which may affect first-layer impedance matching - did not verify exact substrate dataset
What would settle these: look up material_catalog dispersion data for tio2 and sio2, check substrate index, run polarization-resolved simulation
